name: send_intro
description: Sends our standard first text (who we are, that you can book right here by text, the booking link and the front desk number). Use it once, for your first text in a conversation, when the patient greets us, asks who this is, replies to one of our clinic texts, or says they want to book without saying when. Do not use it when their first text already says when (a day, a time, 'asap') or asks something specific, for a lead who is already booked or in review, or when Elliot has already texted in this conversation. Reply INTRO_SENT: the text is already on its way, so do not write any of it yourself, and do not ask about days or times (it already does).

name: find_times
description: Finds open times for the patient's Initial Evaluation. Use it as soon as you know roughly when suits them ('any', 'whatever is soonest', or a plain 'yes' or 'sure' after your day question or a therapist list = when=earliest; 'tomorrow' or 'tmrw' = when=tomorrow), and again for every new day, week, month, time of day, therapist or clinic they ask about; a question like 'anything Thursday?' is always a new search. Never run the same search twice in a row. Offer only times from the latest reply. Reply codes: OPENINGS = times to offer. NOTHING_IN_RANGE = nothing for what they asked; say so and offer the nearest times it lists. A today or tomorrow search reply starts by naming the day searched ('Searched tomorrow, Thu Nov 5'): name that day in your text, never 'today' for another day. NO_OPENINGS = nothing open at all; offer the booking link and the front desk phone (no hand_off unless they ask for a person). NO_SUCH_THERAPIST or NO_OPENINGS_FOR_THERAPIST = name the therapists we have and offer to search without one. NEED_LOCATION = ask which of our clinics they prefer, then search again with clinic. UNKNOWN_LOCATION = not one of our clinics; name ours. PAST_DATE = that day or month has passed; say so and ask for another day (or search when=earliest if they said 'asap'). NEED_DATE, NEED_MONTH, BAD_WHEN or BAD_TIME_OF_DAY = fix that argument and call again; say nothing about it. CASE_CHANGE = they asked for another service than their referral: report_outcome case_change, then hand_off different_case; never search for it. UNKNOWN_SERVICE = we can't search for this patient; use hand_off with reason booking_problem. NO_CLINICIANS = no therapist sees this service at that clinic: if the reply lists clinics after 'Offered at', offer those clinics in one short line and search again with the one they pick (no hand_off); with no 'Offered at', use hand_off with reason booking_problem. REVIEW_OPEN = the patient is waiting for staff review; use hand_off with reason booking_problem. Only a reply containing the words 'too far ahead' means the day is too far ahead to book. For 'how far ahead can I book?', answer only from 'Last bookable day' in a reply. Each time in a reply looks like 'Tuesday, November 3 (2026-11-03) at 9:00 AM with Alan Smith': keep the YYYY-MM-DD date, the time and the therapist's full name for confirm_visit.

when.description: earliest when they gave no day ('anytime', 'asap', only a time of day). specific_date for one named day or date, specific_month for a named month, next_month for 'next month'.

specific_date.description: Only with when=specific_date: the day they named as YYYY-MM-DD, worked out from Now in Context (a day name means the next one on or after today). Otherwise null.

month.description: Only with when=specific_month: the month they named as YYYY-MM. Otherwise null.

time_of_day.description: Only if they asked for a part of the day ('before work' = morning, 'after 5' = evening). Otherwise null.

therapist.description: Only if they asked for a particular therapist: the name as they wrote it. Otherwise null.

clinic.description: Only if they want a different clinic than the one in Context, or for a new person: the clinic they chose. Otherwise null (the clinic in Context).

service.description: Only for someone new (Person texting: someone new) who chose a service: that service as named in Services we book ('pelvic floor' = Physical Therapy - Pelvic). Always null for a patient with a referral: their Service in Context is used, and a different one is a case change.

name: list_therapists
description: Lists the therapists who see this service at a clinic, with short notes. Use it only when the patient asks who the therapists are or asks about one; if a PROVIDERS reply is already in this conversation, answer from it instead. A request to see one ('can I see Alan?') is a search: find_times with therapist. Reply PROVIDERS = the list; name only therapists from it.

clinic.description: Only if it is not the clinic in Context. Otherwise null.

name: check_birthday
description: Checks the date of birth the patient typed against our records (the identity step before the card). Use it in the turn they send their date of birth, with their words as written (or YYYY-MM-DD). Never use it when Context says Date of birth confirmed in this chat: yes. You never see the date on file: never say a date of birth, month, day or year to them. Reply codes: MATCH = it matches; identity done: call confirm_visit now for the time they picked. NEW = noted (no date on file, or someone new); identity done: confirm_visit now (for someone new, once you have their name, clinic and service). CONFIRMED_DIFFERENT = they confirmed a date that differs from our records; we use theirs and staff will see it; identity done: confirm_visit now, say nothing about our records. DIFFERENT = a real date, but not the one on file: ask them once to double-check it, with the words the reply gives; never hint at the date on file. NEED_YEAR = no year: ask once for the year. NOT_POSSIBLE = in the future, less than a year ago or over 120 years ago: ask them kindly to check it and type it again. UNREADABLE = ask them to type it like 3/14/1988.

date_of_birth.description: The patient's date of birth exactly as they typed it in their latest text ('march 14 1988', '3/14/88'), or as YYYY-MM-DD.

name: confirm_visit
description: Checks that a time the patient picked is still open and sends them the visit card (day, time, therapist, clinic, 'Reply YES and I'll book it'). This tool is the only way a card is sent: never write a card, a read-back of the visit or 'I'm holding' yourself. Call it at once when they pick a time: with no date of birth confirmed in this chat yet, it texts our date of birth question naming that time and replies NEED_BIRTH_DATE (add nothing; never ask for the date of birth yourself first). Also call it in the turn the identity step is done (check_birthday replied MATCH, NEW or CONFIRMED_DIFFERENT), unless a Code step note says our system already did. Also call it when book_visit replied NOT_CONFIRMED, or for the same time after a new step (their first name, their date of birth) when the card is no longer your latest text. Book only after this card. Reply codes: CARD_SENT = the card goes out after anything you write; your final answer is NO_REPLY or one short line (a thank-you for their date of birth, or an answer), never a question, never the card's details and never their date of birth. MISSING_NAME = no card was sent: we have no first name on file; ask once "What's your first name?" (never the last name: it is on file), then confirm_visit again for the same time with first_name. NEED_BIRTH_DATE = no card was sent: do what it says (ask once for their date of birth, or once to double-check it), then check_birthday. CARD_ALREADY_SENT = the same card is already your latest text: book_visit on a clear yes, else one short line or NO_REPLY; never ask for anything the card already covers. TAKEN or NOT_AVAILABLE = that time is gone; say so and offer the other times listed. ALREADY_BOOKED = they already have a visit; never book again. REVIEW_OPEN = use hand_off with reason booking_problem. WHICH_THERAPIST = ask the patient which of the therapists it names they mean. NO_SUCH_THERAPIST = name the therapists it lists and offer to search without one. CASE_CHANGE = another service than their referral: report_outcome case_change, then hand_off different_case; never book it. BAD_DATE or BAD_TIME = send the date and time exactly as the find_times reply wrote them.

date.description: The picked day as YYYY-MM-DD, from the parentheses in the find_times reply.

time.description: The picked time exactly as the reply wrote it, for example '9:00 AM'.

therapist.description: The therapist's full name for that time, as the reply wrote it.

clinic.description: The clinic the times were searched at, if not the clinic in Context. Otherwise null.

service.description: Only for someone new: the same service you searched with. Always null for a patient with a referral.

first_name.description: Only when Name on file has no first name: the first name the patient wrote in this chat (never their last name, which is on file). Otherwise null.

name: book_visit
description: Books the Initial Evaluation. Use it when the patient's newest text is a clear yes ('yes', 'yep', 'book it', 'sounds good') to the visit card, and the card is your latest text in the conversation (it starts 'Here's your visit:' and ends 'Reply YES and I'll book it.'; confirm_visit sent it). Call it in that same turn, with exactly the card's date, time, therapist and clinic. Without this tool nothing is booked: never tell the patient they are booked unless this tool replied BOOKED or ALREADY_BOOKED. Our system refuses any other booking (a yes after any other text from you gets NOT_CONFIRMED). Reply codes: BOOKED = done, and our booked text (details and paperwork) is on its way, so never write it yourself. ALREADY_BOOKED = they already have a visit: say only the day, time and therapist the reply gives (if it gives none, use hand_off with reason booking_problem); never book again. TAKEN or NOT_AVAILABLE = the time went; say so and offer the other times listed, then a new card for their new pick. NOT_CONFIRMED = no matching card answered yet; call confirm_visit for that time. IN_PROGRESS ('wait a moment') = an earlier booking is still finishing; call book_visit once more with the same details, and write nothing about waiting. IN_PROGRESS again, ERROR, or an error after IN_PROGRESS = not booked: use hand_off with reason booking_problem and say our front desk will finish setting up the visit; never say it is booked and never offer times again. PATIENT_EXISTS, UNCONFIRMED or FOLLOW_UP = not booked, and our front desk text was already sent; say only that our front desk will finish setting up the visit. REVIEW_OPEN = use hand_off with reason booking_problem. CASE_CHANGE = another service than their referral: report_outcome case_change, then hand_off different_case; never book it. MISSING_NAME = we have no first name: ask once for their first name only (never the last name: it is on file); with their answer call confirm_visit for the same time with first_name, then book_visit after their yes with that first_name. BAD_DATE_OF_BIRTH or BAD_NAME = ask for that detail once, then check_birthday (for a date of birth) and confirm_visit again. HANDED_OFF = booking failed twice for the same reason and our front desk text was sent: ask nothing more about the booking; NO_REPLY or one short line.

time.description: As on the card, for example '9:00 AM'.

therapist.description: The therapist's full name, as on the card.

first_name.description: First name: from Name on file, or as the patient gave it. Never empty.

last_name.description: Last name with a capital first letter: from Name on file, or as the patient gave it. Never empty.

date_of_birth.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the date of birth the patient typed in this chat (check_birthday checked it). Our system books with the date confirmed in this chat, whatever is passed; never guess a year.

clinic.description: As on the card, if not the clinic in Context. Otherwise null.

service.description: Only for someone new: the same service as on the card. Always null for a patient with a referral.

name: report_outcome
description: Records an outcome on the lead so the clinic's lists and calls react. Use it once per outcome, in the same turn as your text about it: callback_scheduled only after the patient said yes to the exact time you confirmed; booking_link when they want to book themselves (the reply gives the link to put in your own text; never use it when Booking link in Context is 'not set'); declined for a plain 'not interested'; do_not_contact when they ask us to stop texting or stop all contact (not for 'stop calling, texting is fine': that is hand_off other); the reply says what was stopped, and your text says only that; wrong_person when they say this is not their number or they don't know the patient; case_change when they want a different service, body part or problem than the referral (call it before hand_off with reason different_case; once per conversation, not again when they ask again). Never use it for a booking (book_visit records that). Reply REPORTED = saved. ALREADY_BOOKED = the patient is booked and nothing changed; answer about their visit. ALREADY_REPORTED = the front desk already has this case change and nothing was sent; say nothing more about it (answer anything else, else NO_REPLY). Any other reply: write your text as planned; our team sees the failure.

status.description: The outcome to record; see the tool description for when each one applies.

notes.description: One short sentence for staff, with no medical details. For case_change only what they asked for, in a word or two, e.g. 'spine', 'pelvic'. For do_not_contact 'stop texts only' or 'asked for no contact at all'.

callback_type.description: Only for callback_scheduled: relative for 'in N minutes or hours' up to 4 hours, absolute for a day, a clock time or anything later. Otherwise null.

delay_minutes.description: Only with callback_type relative: minutes from now, 5 to 240. Otherwise null.

callback_datetime_iso.description: Only with callback_type absolute: the agreed time in clinic time with its offset (-08:00 up to Mar 13 2027, -07:00 from Mar 14 2027 to Nov 6 2027), e.g. '2026-11-03T10:00:00-08:00'. Otherwise null.

name: hand_off
description: Passes the patient to our front desk: sends our front desk text (their phone number, and that they will reach out) and asks the front desk to contact the patient. Use it for anything you do not handle: insurance, cost, billing or coverage (insurance); a different service, body part or problem than the referral, together with report_outcome case_change (different_case); asking for a person or a call from the office (wants_person); writing in another language (other_language, which sends our English-only text instead); a question whose answer is not in your clinic facts, such as parking, directions or which office is closest (unknown_question); a booking that did not go through, or a booking matter while the lead is in review (booking_problem); cancelling or changing a booked visit (cancel_visit, which sends our text that the visit stays booked until the front desk confirms the change); asking us to stop calling while texting is fine, or anything else (other). For insurance, wants_person, other_language, unknown_question, other and cancel_visit, booking by text goes on (the front desk still reaches out). For different_case and booking_problem it puts the lead in review, which pauses booking by text from the next text on, so never offer times after those. If the same text is a clear yes to the card, call book_visit first. Use it once per topic in a conversation: if our front desk text already followed the patient's question on this topic, do not call it again (answer anything else, or NO_REPLY to 'thanks, I'll wait'). For a case change call report_outcome case_change first. Reply HANDED_OFF or HANDED_OFF_PAUSED = the text is on its way, sent before anything you write, so never repeat the phone number or 'they'll reach out'. ALREADY_HANDED_OFF = the front desk already has this and nothing was sent; do not repeat the hand-off (answer anything else they asked, else NO_REPLY), but if they ask how to reach the front desk or to talk to someone, give the phone number the reply gives.

reason.description: Why the front desk is needed; see the tool description for which reason fits.

notes.description: One short sentence for the front desk on what the patient needs, with no medical details, e.g. 'Asked if Blue Shield is accepted.'

name: flag_emergency
description: Sends our fixed 'please call 911' text and alerts our staff. Use it at once when a text suggests a medical emergency or danger right now (chest pain, can't breathe, fainted, fell and can't get up, severe bleeding, thoughts of suicide or self-harm). Not for an injury in the past, like the one that led to the referral. kind: medical for a physical emergency (911 only); self_harm for thoughts of suicide or self-harm (911 and 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline). Once per conversation: if the emergency text is already in the conversation, do not call it again; write one short caring line instead (our team will reach out; please call 911; add 'call or text 988 any time' only for self-harm). Reply EMERGENCY_SENT = sent; your final answer in that turn is NO_REPLY. ALREADY_SENT = it was already sent within the hour (nothing sent again); write that one short line.

kind.description: medical = a physical emergency; self_harm = thoughts of suicide or self-harm.
